newsitem.title: USA: Members of Congress urge Fed not to raise US rates.
newsitem.headline: Members of Congress urge Fed not to raise US rates.

text.p: Some 78 members of Congress Monday urged the Federal Reserve to leave rates unchanged when the Federal Open Market Committee meets Tuesday.

In a letter to the Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan, the group, which included Minority Leader Dick Gephardt (D-Mo) said that it would be unwise to raise rates at a time when inflation seems benign and the government is holding the line on spending.
"As we look at the current economic situation, we think the Fed should not raise rates due to the negative consequences that action could have for the national economy," the letter said.
It added that as the budget deficit shrinks and budget plans continue to reduce federal procurement and employment, fiscal policy will have a contractionary effect in the near term.
"A rate increase would provide an additional contractionary influence that may force the economy into a downturn during a critical period of time," the letter said.
